question: Would you trust an assistant to spend your money for you?
reflection: Convenience should never cost us our sense of control; good design protects both.

sources.subject: 1980s energy model beats modern AI loops by 1,000x in speed

one_line: Chip export rules look leakier than hoped, while AI assistants take their first real steps toward paying for things on our behalf.

top_stories.title: Top Chinese models reportedly trained on banned chips
top_stories.what: Analysis of published model weights suggests DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group trained new models on Nvidia Blackwell chips that the US bars from export to China.
top_stories.why: If hardware controls leak this much, policy advice on AI supply chains should not rely on chips alone as the lever.

top_stories.title: ChatGPT can now pay at checkout
top_stories.what: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet for some US users, letting its agent use a saved card once the user approves a purchase or grants advance permission.
top_stories.why: Letting AI spend money raises fresh questions about consent, impulse buying and trust that behavioural research is well placed to study.

top_stories.title: OpenAI folds robotics into its main models
top_stories.what: OpenAI reportedly closed its stand-alone robotics team, betting that its general models can increasingly control machines without a separate robot model.
top_stories.why: It signals that the same AI behind chatbots may soon run physical devices, from warehouses to hospital logistics.

saudi_lens.text: Evidence that restricted chips still reach China may push Washington to tighten checks on all buyers, which could slow chip deliveries to Saudi data-centre projects.
Agent-led payments will need clear rules from local regulators before such features reach Saudi shoppers.

idea.title: Consent design for AI purchases
idea.pitch: Test different approval screens for AI-made purchases and measure which ones keep users in control without making them abandon useful tasks.
idea.fit: Consumer protection bodies, fintech regulators, consultancy
idea.first_step: Sketch three approval flows (every purchase, spending limit, weekly summary) and draft a short online experiment comparing them.

idea_kids.title: Ask before you buy
idea_kids.pitch: A role-play kit where children practise when to ask a parent before buying online, including in games and apps.
idea_kids.first_step: Write 8 short shopping situations with 'ask' or 'okay' answers.

terms.definition: Government rules limiting which countries or companies can buy certain technologies, such as advanced AI chips.
The learned numbers inside an AI model that hold what it has learned; publishing them lets others run the model.
Purchases that an AI agent completes for a person, using a saved card under limits the person sets.

concepts.summary: Rules deciding which countries and companies can access advanced AI chips.
Designing services so AI agents can complete them on a person's behalf.
Using the same large models behind chatbots to steer physical machines.
